newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait Petroleum net profit projected higher.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait Petroleum net profit projected higher.

text.p: A parliamentary committee has approved a 1997/98 budget for Kuwait Petroleum Corp with a projected net profit of 671.61 million dinars ($2.22 billion), up from 570.72 million dinars for 1996/97.
The financial committee approved the budget and referred it to the full parliament, a statement by the panel said, after agreeing with KPC officials to cut projected spending by 2.25 million dinars.

Budget forecasts put revenue at 3.973 billion dinars for the current fiscal year which started on July 1 compared with 3.860 billion for 1996/97. Spending was put at 3.301 billion dinars compared with 3.289 billion the previous year.

Kuwait has in recent years calculated oil revenue at a conservative $13.5 a barrel while Kuwaiti crudes averaged some $5 a barrel above that in 1996. It has a domestic refining capacity of about 895,000 barrels per day (bpd) in addition to a downstream network and refineries abroad.
Oil prices are some 30 percent lower than the end of 1996 when exporters recorded higher-than-forecast income.

Kuwait, which controls about 10 percent of world reserves, produces about two million bpd. KPC's budget was calculated at Kuwait's Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) two-million-bpd quota.
Salaries and benefits at state-owned KPC, a key employer of Kuwaitis, were estimated at 239 million dinars for 1997/98 compared with 232 million the previous year.
KPC, one of the world's 10 largest oil firms, owns companies which produce, refine and market oil and petrochemicals and explore for oil and gas internationally, and runs an oil tanker business.
* Slight discrepancies in figures are due to rounding.
